text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"Incorporating the periodic consolidation technique described in the arXiv paper (0a553296) into the Structured Memory Rewrite pipeline should reduce cross‑fact interference and yield higher downstream recall than a pure rewrite‑only approach, suggesting a hybrid rewrite‑plus‑consolidation method that can be empirically tested against the current baseline.","confidence":0.74,"support_ids":["61f4d4ec","0a553296","8e3bb063"],"tags":["memory‑consolidation","rewrite‑vs‑append","hybrid‑method"]},{"statement":"Applying the agent‑memory benchmark framework being drafted with Maya (303fb425) provides a ready‑made ablation platform to compare rewrite operations against a naive append baseline, and its existing performance metrics can predict how memory‑size variations will affect the ICLR paper’s reported gains, thereby directly addressing Reviewer 2’s concern.","confidence":0.69,"support_ids":["61f4d4ec","303fb425"],"tags":["benchmark","ablation","memory‑size"]}]}
